newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury U.S. unit buys stores from Ahold.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury U.S. unit buys stores from Ahold.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc said on Monday its U.S. unit Shaw's Supermarkets had agreed to buy 12 stores and two sites in the U.S. from Royal Ahold for $52 million in cash.
Sainsbury said in a statement that all the locations were in Connecticut except for one site in Rhode Island.
Sainsbury said the purchase would up Shaw's presence to 18 stores in Connecticut and place it second in the market, "as well as providing significant operating and marketing economies."
Shaw's chairman Ian Coull said the deal was "at a cost which will enable us to make a very satisfactory return."
Sainsbury confirmed in August that it was discussing purchase of around 12 stores with Ahold after a report in the Sunday Telegraph newspaper, but declined to put a value on the deal.
The Sunday Telegraph said on August 11 that the deal could be worth up to 50 million stg.
Deputy chief executive Dino Adriano told Reuters at the end of August that the group would be happy to clinch the U.S. deal because it wanted to expand in America.
He said then the size of the U.S. market meant that "the opportunity for getting a formula right and then rolling it out...is quite significant."
